newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end firm on insitutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end firm on insitutional buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly firmer on Wednesday on institutional buying, while turnover was supported by foreign buying of two brewery scrips, brokers said.

The Colombo all share index closed 0.59 points higher at 614.96. Price gains and losses ran neck and neck at 16 each. Shares of Lanka Walltile rose one rupee to 26 and those of Lanka Orix Leasing fell two rupees to 149.
"Though investors who trade are waiting to see if election violence will affect prices, institutional investors will buy if you can show them a good quantity," said a broker at John Keells.
Last week's shooting of a ruling party legislator a day before nominations closed for local government polls on March 21, has sent many investors to the sidelines, brokers said.
Turnover was 21 million rupees, on foreign buying of 98,800 Ceylon Brewery and 170,200 Lion Brewery.

Foreign buying was worth 10.8 million rupees, and selling was 4.2 million. "There was foreign interest in both shares. We were lucky that buying and selling just happened to match today," said Rohan Fernando, a broker at CT Smith Stock Brokers.
